description.short_caption: Multiple ulcerative skin lesions with crusting on the lower extremity.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows multiple ulcerative lesions on the skin of the lower extremity. The lesions are round to oval, with central crusting and surrounding erythema. The distribution appears scattered, and the lesions vary in size. The surrounding skin shows no significant swelling or discoloration beyond the erythematous margins of the ulcers.

description.short_caption: Multiple pustules and crusted lesions on the forehead.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the forehead of a patient with numerous pustules, some of which are crusted or healing. The lesions are distributed across the forehead, with varying sizes and stages of development. The skin surrounding the lesions appears mildly erythematous. No other parts of the face are visible in this image.

description.short_caption: Ulcerated lesion with central necrosis and surrounding erythema on the skin.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a single ulcerated lesion on the skin. The lesion has a central area of necrosis with a dark eschar, surrounded by a rim of erythema. The surrounding skin appears intact, with no obvious satellite lesions. The lesion is well-demarcated and appears to be slightly raised at the edges.

description.short_caption: Facial lesion near the lower lip with surrounding beard area.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower face of an individual, focusing on the perioral region. A raised, ulcerated lesion with a crusted surface is visible on the left side of the beard area below the lower lip. The surrounding skin appears slightly erythematous. The lips themselves appear unremarkable, and there is no visible discharge from the lesion.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of biopsy showing epithelial and subepithelial layers.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of epithelial tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The upper portion demonstrates a stratified squamous epithelium with a dense, darkly stained layer of cells, while the lower portion reveals the subepithelial connective tissue with a looser, lighter staining pattern. The tissue architecture is preserved, and no obvious signs of necrosis or significant inflammatory infiltrates are visible.
visible_findings: H&E staining with distinct purple and pink hues

description.short_caption: H&E stain of skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia and dermal inflammation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section of skin. The epidermis demonstrates hyperplasia with elongation of rete ridges. The dermis contains a dense inflammatory infiltrate, predominantly composed of lymphocytes. The overall architecture suggests a chronic inflammatory process. No organisms are directly visible in this stain.

description.short_caption: Histopathology showing spirochetes in a tissue sample stained with Warthin-Starry silver stain.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image demonstrates a tissue section stained with Warthin-Starry silver stain, highlighting spirochetes (indicated by arrows) as thin, dark, spiral-shaped organisms. The background shows a dense inflammatory infiltrate with numerous cells, likely representing a host immune response. The spirochetes are distributed in the tissue, consistent with an infectious etiology such as syphilis. The stain enhances the visibility of these organisms against the cellular background.
